The daily field guide for digital media

AI Media Scout

2026-11-09 · All platforms · Open-source software

Expanded open-source creative-AI discovery across 94 fields, 808 repository queries and 22 model tasks, with primary web research beyond GitHub. This edition completes earlier screened guides, adds newly screened creative workflows and records substantive JoyAI/HME/BeatDesign updates without calling them new launches. Source review only; no discovered application was installed or run. Weekly current-source review covers all 1,990 previously published entries; missing evidence remains explicit and prior reports are preserved. The pending appendix contains screened software/creative-AI relevance only, not full setup or quality recommendations. Raw, unreviewed, excluded and duplicate-only candidates stay local. Additional primary-site follow-up screened 17 source repositories: 6 had reviewed open-source grants and supported workflows, 6 had restricted current code and 5 had unresolved complete-grant evidence. Those outcomes are recorded separately from search-query coverage. Verified collection: 808/808 repository queries attempted; 808 successful, 0 partial, 0 failed and 126 bounded/truncated. All 22 model tasks were attempted; 0 failed. These are bounded discovery attempts, not an exhaustive census or quality approval. Separate from successful search queries, 39 watchlist fetches and 3 enrichment attempts failed; the detailed warnings remain in the report. A 404/409 is an availability gap, not proof of abandonment or license revocation.

Search and review counts

94 creative fields; 808/808 repository queries attempted; 22/22 model-task queries attempted. 31286 distinct source candidates and 919 model leads. 26 detailed profiles and 207 additional screened discoveries. Source gaps: 0 failed repository queries, 0 partial repository queries, 126 bounded repository queries, 0 failed model-task queries and 0 web ecosystem gaps. Raw search candidates include duplicates of known tools, excluded projects and projects awaiting review; they are not verified recommendations.

Profiles are based on current primary documentation. Creative quality and performance claims are attributed to the developers unless hands-on testing is explicitly recorded. Unknown hardware requirements stay unknown. Code, model weights, hosted services, and required proprietary hosts can have different terms.

Install

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.

git clone https://github.com/Saquib764/photo-organiser-ai.git
cd photo-organiser-ai/backend
uv sync
uv run uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001
cd ../frontend
yarn install
yarn build
yarn preview

What it is good for

Art-direct a diffusion composition with structured noise, compare neighboring variations, and explore controlled image/video noise patterns. [1]

Demo & examples

Install

Install ComfyUI separately, use Manager to install ComfyUI-ShaderNoiseKSampler or clone it into custom_nodes, then restart ComfyUI. The node documents no extra pip dependencies. [1]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. Install ComfyUI separately, use Manager to install ComfyUI-ShaderNoiseKSampler or clone it into custom_nodes, then restart ComfyUI. The node documents no extra pip dependencies.
git clone https://github.com/AEmotionStudio/ComfyUI-ShaderNoiseKSampler.git

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1]

  1. Add Shader Noise KSampler (Direct) in place of KSampler and connect model, conditioning and latent inputs.
  2. Keep the seed fixed, choose the explore preset and start with low shader strength.
  3. Inspect the live shader preview, queue a short test and compare nearby settings before expanding the experiment.
  4. Use standard sampling for a new graph; inspect older workflows that load legacy mode.

docker compose build

Separately configure TouchDesigner to use the td-ml environment through TDPyEnvManager, excluding pyEDFlib from the runtime environment. Read the model/data restrictions before using or redistributing included joblib files. [1] [3]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. Clone this repository, create a Python 3.10+ environment and install requirements. Separately configure TouchDesigner to use the td-ml environment through TDPyEnvManager, excluding pyEDFlib from the runtime environment. Read the model/data restrictions before using or redistributing included joblib files.
git clone https://github.com/raystermomo/NeuroCanvas.git
cd NeuroCanvas
python -m venv .venv
pip install -r requirements.txt

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1] [3]

  1. Activate the environment with the documented command for your OS and configure the separate TouchDesigner environment.
  2. Set Mind Monitor Raw EEG /muse/eeg streaming to the computer IP and port 5005 on the same WiFi.
  3. Open EEG2Emotion_Visual.toe; enable OSC Time Slice and map four channels exactly TP9 AF7 AF8 TP10.
  4. Point VA_Infer at the model and code directory, inspect incoming data, calibrate and connect valence/arousal to the visual synthesizer.
  5. Treat movement as an artistic control signal; compare mappings and inspect the output before a live presentation.

Hardware & software

Requirements below are documented for this workflow. Unspecified limits are not inferred. [1] [3]

Hardware
Muse 2 EEG headset, a Mind Monitor phone and a computer on the same WiFi are documented. Minimum RAM, GPU/VRAM, storage and measured end-to-end latency are not documented.
Software
Python 3.10+, NumPy/SciPy, LightGBM, scikit-learn, joblib and the documented TD-ML environment; TouchDesigner and TDPyEnvManager. pyEDFlib is required for raw-data training, not the dependency-light runtime feature extractor.
Platforms
The guide provides shell and Windows activation examples but no tested operating-system/TouchDesigner-version matrix. A browser or Python script does not establish Linux support for the complete TouchDesigner workflow.

License, model weights & costs

The full software license was reviewed. Model weights, assets and services remain separate. [2] [1] [3]

  • Weights: Complete MIT software grant reviewed. TouchDesigner, Mind Monitor and Muse hardware are separate. The README says NeuroSense data and derivatives are subject to a restrictive Data Use Agreement while also shipping a trained model; rights to redistribute or commercially reuse that checkpoint are unresolved. TD-ML has its own MIT attribution.
  • Commercial: Software use follows MIT. Complete MIT software grant reviewed. TouchDesigner, Mind Monitor and Muse hardware are separate. The README says NeuroSense data and derivatives are subject to a restrictive Data Use Agreement while also shipping a trained model; rights to redistribute or commercially reuse that checkpoint are unresolved. TD-ML has its own MIT attribution.
  • Cost: Muse hardware, phone/app and any required TouchDesigner license plus local compute. Current prices and commercial checkpoint clearance are not established.

Why it merits attention

Included for the documented creative workflow. A complete guide and popularity do not establish output reliability. [1] [3]

Limitations

The main README describes16-second windows and a2-second training step, while the detailed TD guide describes a4-second inference buffer and SVR/LightGBM averaging; these documents conflict. The detailed guide reports weak cross-subject CCC around0.17/0.08 and middle-biased output. Personal calibration may improve range but is not proof of emotion accuracy. No AI Media Scout execution or biological-signal validation was performed. [1] [3]

git clone https://github.com/jd-opensource/JoyAI-Video-Edit.git

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1] [3] [4] [5]

  1. Complete the documented environment/kernel steps before downloading the chosen models.
  2. Place joyai_video_edit_dit_1101_face++.pth, VAE and MiMo-VL in the documented checkpoint tree.
  3. Use the hardware-specific launcher from DEPLOYMENT.md; the 5090 route disables local prompt enhancement. Set JOYOMNI_HOST=127.0.0.1 when local-only access is intended.
  4. Load a short clip or camera and authorized reference, request a character change, then inspect identity, source motion, temporal drift and export.

Hardware & software

Requirements below are documented for this workflow. Unspecified limits are not inferred. [1] [3] [4] [5]

Hardware
Owner-tested RTX 5090 32 GB at 840×480/24 FPS; video-only low-VRAM layout measured about 21.5 GiB resident and 28 GiB peak under a 30 GiB allocator cap. Full 720p/16 FPS layout needs about 46.5 GB steady. B200 reaches the separate reported 720p/30 FPS configuration. RAM and total required storage are not documented; optional Qwen weights alone add about 20.4 GiB.
Software
Linux x86_64, Python 3.10, PyTorch 2.9.1 CUDA 12.8 wheels and nvcc 12.8+ for Blackwell. Compiled joyomni_ops, Triton and GPU-specific attention configuration are required. FA4 B200 and patched SageAttention RTX 5090 routes differ.

Linux/NVIDIA deployment is documented. Native macOS and Windows operation is not established by the browser client.

First project

git clone --recursive https://github.com/OpenImageDenoise/oidn.git
oidnDenoise -h

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1]

  1. Install Git LFS before cloning; otherwise model/source files can be invalid even when Git reports success.
  2. Use the released library/example or follow the exact backend-specific build guide; inspect oidnDenoise help for available options.
  3. Prepare a noisy render and matching optional albedo/normal AOVs. Default CLI input is little-endian PFM; OpenEXR/PNG need an OpenImageIO-enabled rebuild.
  4. Select the correct HDR/filter settings and inspect fine detail and sequences against a higher-sample reference before integrating the output.

Hardware & software

Requirements below are documented for this workflow. Unspecified limits are not inferred. [1]

Hardware
CPU requires x64 with SSE4.1 or ARM64. GPU is optional and backend-specific. No universal RAM/VRAM or total-disk minimum is established; render size and buffers determine memory use.
Software
v2.5.1 documented. 64-bit OS and x64 SSE4.1 or ARM64 CPU. Optional GPU backend requirements differ for Intel SYCL, NVIDIA CUDA, AMD HIP and Apple Metal; training is a separate Linux/Python/PyTorch workflow and is not needed for bundled inference.
Platforms
64-bit Windows/Linux/macOS. Apple GPU requires macOS Ventura+. Documented GPU families include Intel Xe-series, NVIDIA Turing/Ampere/Ada/Hopper/Blackwell, AMD RDNA2–4 and Apple M1+. Check the exact current driver table rather than assuming every GPU works.

License, model weights & costs

The full software license was reviewed. Model weights, assets and services remain separate. [2] [1]

  • Weights: Complete Apache-2.0 software grant, including patent/NOTICE/redistribution conditions, was compared in full. Optional drivers, rendering hosts, third-party components and user-trained model/data rights remain separate. This review does not clear redistribution of every custom checkpoint.
  • Commercial: Software use follows Apache-2.0. Complete Apache-2.0 software grant, including patent/NOTICE/redistribution conditions, was compared in full. Optional drivers, rendering hosts, third-party components and user-trained model/data rights remain separate. This review does not clear redistribution of every custom checkpoint.
  • Cost: Local compute and any chosen renderer/driver stack. Apache code does not require an OIDN subscription; host licensing is separate.

Why it merits attention

Included for the documented creative workflow. A complete guide and popularity do not establish output reliability. [1]

Limitations

Denoising can lose detail or introduce artifacts; a fast preview is not ground truth. Auxiliary-buffer conventions, device memory, GPU buffer APIs and image-format support matter. A renderer must use its actual integrated version. Universal RAM/VRAM/disk minima were not established in this review. [1]

How it uses AI

A local text/vision model refines image prompts and plans scenes, while connected Forge/ComfyUI backends generate stills and Wan2GP optionally animates them. The November 9 v6.0 release adds model presets, creative LoRA selection and recorded per-scene animation settings. [1] [3]

Introduction

A local text/vision model refines image prompts and plans scenes, while connected Forge/ComfyUI backends generate stills and Wan2GP optionally animates them. The November 9 v6.0 release adds model presets, creative LoRA selection and recorded per-scene animation settings. [1] [3]

What it is good for

Develop a character or storyboard, compare prompts against one seed, and build a short music-backed scene sequence while retaining each scene’s settings. The scoped video workflow requires separately installed generation backends. [1] [3]

Demo & examples

The README supplies UI screenshots and the official v6.0 release describes an owner-tested FastWan 5B workflow on an 8 GB GPU. Gallery, A/B, auto-refine, LoRA and image-to-prompt screenshot images are explicitly abstract placeholders; all screenshots use demo data. They are not independent output-quality evidence. [1] [3]

Install

Python 3.10+ is documented. On Windows, inspect and use the repository’s install.bat, then run.bat. macOS/Linux use install.sh and run.sh and are explicitly less tested. Configure a local text/vision provider and an existing Forge/ComfyUI installation; add FFmpeg and Wan2GP only for the selected video route. Setup can download models, while the v6 animation preflight itself is offline. [1] [3]

Setup can download models, while the v6 animation preflight itself is offline.
git clone https://github.com/Kisahime/promptmaker.git
cd promptmaker
install.bat
run.bat

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1] [3]

  1. Use the displayed commands on Windows; macOS/Linux use the separately documented ./install.sh and ./run.sh routes.
  2. Choose Settings → AI provider, test the actual local text/vision models and connect an existing image backend with a licensed checkpoint.
  3. For Video maker, plan a few scenes, edit prompts, lengths and captions, then make and inspect stills before animating selected scenes.
  4. Select the installed Wan2GP preset and optional creative LoRA; inspect missing-file and compatibility warnings and start with a short scene.
  5. Build the MP4 with FFmpeg and review every frame, caption and music right. Preserve scene settings and project files before upgrading.

Hardware & software

Requirements below are documented for this workflow. Unspecified limits are not inferred. [1] [3]

Hardware
No universal RAM, VRAM or total-disk minimum is documented. The owner reports FastWan 5B at 1280×704/121 frames on an 8 GB GPU; other presets can need more. Optional LoRA training separately needs NVIDIA: an 8 GB preset is documented, 16 GB+ recommended, with about 6 GB trainer setup before datasets/checkpoints.
Software
Python 3.10+, PySide6 and keyring; face masks add OpenCV/onnxruntime. Local Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible text/vision server is optional; actual image generation needs Forge/A1111 with its API or ComfyUI. Video assembly needs FFmpeg; animation needs a compatible Wan2GP version with --offline support and downloaded models. Linux Qt runtime libraries are listed in the README.
Platforms
Windows is the main documented install. macOS/Linux should work according to the developer but are less tested; that does not verify every GPU backend on those systems. A headless UI test is not cross-platform model execution.
